problem.title: Long-Running Batch Job Replaced Mid-Flight Without State Checkpoint

requirements: Operational Invariant: "Batch processing jobs must persist periodic checkpoint progress to enable resume-from-failure after pod terminations."

Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.

referenceMaterial.summary: Architect long-running batch jobs to be idempotent and checkpointed: save progress state periodically (e.g. after every 10,000 records) to database/S3, and handle SIGTERM gracefully by flushing the latest checkpoint before exit. Invariant: "Batch processing jobs must persist periodic checkpoint progress to enable resume-from-failure after pod terminations."
approachSteps: 1. Ingress Boundary Defense: Architect long-running batch jobs to be idempotent and checkpointed: save progress state periodically (e.g. after every 10,000 records) to database/S3
2. Failure Containment: Eliminate unconstrained buffering and propagate physical backpressure.
3. Invariant Enforcement: Batch processing jobs must persist periodic checkpoint progress to enable resume-from-failure after pod terminations.
referenceMaterial.diagramDescription: Ingress → Bounded Admission Controller → Adaptive Concurrency / Queue Gate → Protected Worker Engine; Overload Shed Path → HTTP 429 / Circuit Fallback (<0.1ms).

stages.learnerPrompt: Compare naive architecture vs production-hardened patterns. Walk through the key trade-offs and operational attributes.

referenceMaterial.summary: Architectural comparison of naive unconstrained allocations versus production-hardened mechanical sympathy.
tradeOffs: Ingress Admission: Naive unconstrained buffering causes queue bloat and GC exhaustion. Mitigation: Bounded ingress gate with fast non-blocking shedding.
Resource Strategy: Static capacity allocations collapse under brownouts. Mitigation: Dynamic adaptive limits scaling to real-time physical bounds.
Outage Impact: Cascading lock convoys and memory saturation. Mitigation: Isolated failure domains keep P99 latency flat and protected.
alternatives: Naive Approach: Deployment terminates the pod at hour 5. The job aborts without saving intermediate state. The new pod restarts from hour 0, missing business morning
Production-Hardened Pattern: Architect long-running batch jobs to be idempotent and checkpointed: save progress state periodically (e.g. after every 10,000 records) to database/S3

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Scale Surge → Unbounded Contention → Physical Bottleneck → 💥 Outage Cascade.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Deployment terminates the pod at hour 5. The job aborts without saving intermediate state. The new pod restarts from hour 0, missing business morning deadlines and calculating duplicate intermediate balances.
Breakdown Chain: Scale Surge → Unbounded Contention → Physical Bottleneck → 💥 Outage Cascade
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

stages.learnerPrompt: How does the system enforce physical resource boundaries under sudden downstream latency brownouts?

referenceMaterial.summary: Senior Staff SRE Interview challenge and architectural invariant verification.
tradeOffs: Architectural Invariant: "Batch processing jobs must persist periodic checkpoint progress to enable resume-from-failure after pod terminations."
Physical Resource Boundary: Dynamic admission control ensures worker threads never buffer dead requests during downstream brownouts.
approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
